After [him], Ptolemy Epiphanes, that is,
the Purifier (or Conqueror?), twenty-one years;
and in other copies, twenty-four.
This man sent Scopas, his commander-in-chief, and conquered Judah and Syria.
And that Antiochus the Great went out against him,
and defeated the army of the Egyptians,
and took all the cities from them.
Now the Jews readily submitted to Antiochus,
and he honored them with gifts,
and he paved roads and causeways across which armies march,
and he built stone bridges over the rivers.
And in the eleventh year of Antiochus the Great himself, he was defeated by the Romans at Thermopylae,
and he agreed to give them annually a thousand talents of gold,
and he also gave his son, that Antiochus Epiphanes, to the Romans as a hostage.
And from then on the kingdom of the Greeks was subjugated under the hand of the Romans.
And for this reason the Greeks and the Egyptians were united with one another,
and Antiochus canceled the war with Ptolemy Epiphanes,
and made friendship with him.
And that Antiochus the Great took Cleopatra, the daughter of Ptolemy Epiphanes, as his wife {OCR?},
and he gave Syria, Phoenicia, Samaria, and Judah as her dowry.
And in the seventeenth year of Ptolemy Epiphanes, Antiochus the Great {OCR: 'the Great'} went down against Elam, the royal city of the Persians,
and there he died,
